Dinner for 20 (Ski Trip)
So I will be cooking for my organization's ski trip. I'm not a big fan of skiing but I wanted to go and spend time with my friends, so I volunteered for this task. It's always been a dream to cook a big meal like this for my friends and I think I'm a pretty good home cook, so I'm super excited! But, I just want some feedback on my menu.

​

Here's what I'm thinking:

\-chili (with meat, beans, corn, some veg - might make two seperate batches so I can make a spicy version)

\-mac and cheese (not 100% sure on this one because cheese is expensive/not great where I live, but I could stretch it a little with a cream sauce)

\-ratatouille (small portion - there's at least one vegetarian attending, maybe more)

\-non-dairy carb (might just make some white rice for the lactose intolerant folks)

\-cucumber salad (cucumbers are cheap here and I think something crunchy will be a nice pairing... also leftovers will hold up better than a lettuce salad)

\-beer bread (I make this for like every event and it's usually the first thing gone)

\-dessert (I want to try to make red velvet cake since it's two of my friends birthdays and they both said they like red velvet but I've never made it before! Buttermilk isn't available here so I will have to improvise a little.)

​

One of my worries is that there might not be an oven available. I'll find out later this week if there's one at the venue. The only thing that would \*really\* affect is the bread and dessert, so I'm not too worried. The other recipes can be adjusted.

​

Here's my questions:

1. How do I do chili math? I've only really cooked chili at home and for potlucks, so I'm a bit worried about having enough for everyone. I don't want anyone to go hungry!
2. Should I try to make mac and cheese for the crowd? The only cheese here (that's not out of budget) is bagged shredded cheese. I usually make a pretty good mac and cheese with it by mixing it with a bechamel sauce.
3. What are some desserts that I could make without an oven?
4. What are some batch cocktail recipes that will go well with this menu?

​

Thank you for reading!!!

Loaded Avocado Baked Eggs

There are a couple of “tricks” to perfecting this recipe, however. For starters, use large avocados and medium-sized eggs. Otherwise, the egg white may overflow the avocado. Cracking each egg into a small bowl before carefully pouring it into the avocado will also help prevent spills. 

Tip: To keep your egg-filled avocados from tipping over while baking, position them over the holes of a muffin tin, rather than on a flat baking sheet, before placing them in the oven. 

Prep time: 5 minutes
Cook time: 20 - 25 minutes
Serves: 4

Ingredients:

2 large ripe avocados 
4 medium eggs
Sea salt and black pepper, to taste
½ c. Cheddar Jack Cheese, shredded 
3 strips sugar-free bacon, cooked crispy and crumbled

Optional garnish: chives or green onions (green parts only), sliced thin 

Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 350° F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. 

2. Cut avocados in half lengthwise and remove the pits. Use a spoon to carefully remove some of the avocado flesh around the pit to create more space for the egg. Reserve removed flesh for another use (or smash, season with salt and pepper to taste, and top each baked avocado half with a spoonful before serving). 

3. Crack one egg into a small bowl and then carefully transfer the egg into one of the prepared avocado halves. Place the filled avocado onto the prepared baking sheet and repeat this process with the remaining avocado halves and eggs. Season each with salt and black pepper, to taste. 

4. Place filled avocado halves in pre-heated oven to bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the eggs are cooked according to your preference. 

5. Remove from oven and top each avocado half with shredded Cheddar Jack cheese and crispy bacon pieces. Garnish with chives or sliced green onions, if desired, and serve immediately. Enjoy! 

Carbs/Serving:

Total carbs: 7.9 g
Fiber: 5.9 g
Net carbs: 2 g

Mini Egg Muffins
**Originally recipe is here :** [Mini Egg Muffins](https://healtyanddeliciousfood.com/mini-egg-muffins/)

You can eat it anytime, because the estimated calorie content of 1 muffin is 60 calories. You can eat these muffins, which you can prepare in a short time, as an afternoon snack, before or after sports. You can prepare about 6 muffins with this mixture. Instead of olive oil, you can use any other vegetable oil that suits your taste.

Prep Time       :  10 Minutes
Cooking Time : 20 Minutes
Total Time       : 30 Minutes
Calories           : 1 Per 60 kcal
Serving            : 6 Muffins

*Note: From the recipe you get 6 muffins. If you want less or more, you can increase or decrease the number of ingredients.*

INGREDIENTS

* 2 eggs
* 2 eggs white
* 1/2 cup chopped mushrooms
* 1 tablespoon paprika
* 1 tablespoon green pepper
* 1 sprig fresh garlic
* 2 spring onions
* Half a bunch of spinach
* Black pepper
* Salt
* Fat-free cottage cheese (optional)

## DIRECTIONS

* Fry the spring onions and peppers in a wok pan to which you add olive oil.
* Then add the spinach and then the mushrooms and continue stirring.
* Add the fresh garlic and the spices
* Beat the eggs and egg whites in a separate bowl and add them to the prepared vegetable mixture.
* Add the cheese mixture to the obtained egg-vegetable mixture, pour into the muffin cups and bake in a preheated oven at 180 degrees for 20 minutes.
* After removing from the oven, let cool for a while and serve.

So one of the best things to do if you love Asian food and have a bunch of cucumbers to get rid of is to make **cucumber kimchi**. You can make a big batch at once and portion it out over a relatively long time because it keeps longer than fresh. The outsides of the chopped cukes will soften as they absorb flavor, but the insides will maintain most of the crisp as long as you don't dice too finely.

Onions Baked In Marsala (Cipolle al forno alla Marsala)

8 red onions

16 whole cloves, or 1/2 teaspoon of ground cloves

a handful of fresh thyme

3 fresh bay leaves

150 ml / 3 cup dry Marsala or dry sherry

3 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil

sea salt and freshly ground black pepper


Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) Gas 4.
Cut the onions in half and stud each half with cloves.

Arrange in a single layer on a baking dish and add water to reach halfway up the onions. Sprinkle over the thyme sprigs and bay leaves. 

Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes in the preheated oven. The onions should be tender and the water should have evaporated - this will very much depend on the size of your onions, and their freshness etc. so keep checking that the onions are not drying out.

Remove the onions from the oven and remove the cloves. Pour over the Marsala and bake for another 20 minutes, uncovered.

Season with salt and pepper and anoint with fine oil. Serve on their own, with other vegetables as antipasti or to accompany meats.

Well, I have not made what you are talking about, specifically, but when I want to raw add vegetables to things without adding as much water, I will salt and press them.  For grated onions in meatballs, cucumber in tzatziki and so on.

Mince or grate whatever it is, salt generously (you may want to use a portion of the salt that goes into the bread recipe so the final product is not oversalted).  Get some plates that nest together and put one upside down on a baking sheet.  Put the vegetables on the bottom of the plate and put another upside down plate on top of them.  Repeat layers of plates if necessary.  Put something heavy on top; I usually use a cast iron dutch oven.

In a couple/few hours, most of the water should have bled out and collected in the baking sheet.  You can put the remaining vegetables in cheese cloth, a towel or whatever, and squeeze it out even further if needed.  Cucumber will reduce 90% in volume so it is pretty effective on soft/watery vegetables.  Hard ones like root vegetables don't work as well.
